function.name: update_intake
function.description: Save newly supplied facts BEFORE asking the next question, even when most fields are missing. One save per caller turn containing everything that turn said, with the caller's own words as caller_quote. A clear AC outage saves cooling_unavailable=true, service_type=repair, service_category=hvac and issue_summary in the first update; a heat outage uses heating_unavailable=true. Save volunteered vulnerability or cold indoors in that same update. One sequential call using the latest state.revision. Fact fields go inside changes (top-level facts are moved there and listed in moved_into_place). Save values first; read them back and END YOUR TURN; confirm only in a later update after the caller says yes (address and callback may be confirmed together). Confirmation sends address_confirmed/callback_confirmed in changes plus confirmation_address/confirmation_callback copied from the saved state (top level; also accepted inside changes). A confirmation whose caller_quote is your own readback, or that arrives in the same turn the value was saved, returns needs_caller_yes. A covered NYC ZIP fills city and state automatically; never ask the state. The response carries triage (level, priority_tier, missing_risk_fields, ask_next), readiness and a bounded membership result. The backend prefills an unconfirmed callback from caller ID and, after a unique name/phone match, an unconfirmed saved address; changing the street of that saved address clears its old unit and ZIP. Weather triage is automatic. For a current gas smell, CO alarm, smoke/burning smell or sparking use report_safety_emergency FIRST instead. This tool does not book or dispatch. Any result that isn't a success has status, missing, expected (exact saved values to echo) and a one-sentence hint: follow the hint and never speak past it as if it worked. stop_retrying means stop calling this tool: record request_followup(reason=technical_issue) and tell the caller the team will follow up.

expected_revision.description: 0 for the first update; otherwise use state.revision from the latest tool result.

caller_quote.description: Short quote of what the CALLER actually said supporting these changes (for a confirmation, their yes, e.g. "Yes, that's right"). Never your own readback; never invent a quote.

service_address.description: Street number and street name only. Save apartment/unit and ZIP separately. Do not guess or silently change the address.

address_confirmed.description: True only after you read the saved street, unit and ZIP back, ended your turn, and the caller said yes in a later turn. Do not change address components in this update.

service_type.description: Classify the requested service; maintenance can still reveal an urgent risk.

heating_unavailable.description: Caller reports loss of heat. Use unknown if explicitly uncertain; omit if not discussed.

cooling_unavailable.description: Caller reports AC not producing cooling, including not turning on. Use unknown if explicitly uncertain; omit if not discussed.

cold_conditions_reported.description: Caller reports cold or winter conditions relevant to the loss of heat. Do not infer weather solely from the date. Use unknown if explicitly uncertain; omit if not discussed.

vulnerable_resident.description: Answer to the one neutral question asked for every heating/cooling outage: is anyone at home who'd be at higher risk (older adult, infant/young child, health condition)? true or false from the caller's answer; 'unknown' if they don't know or prefer not to say. Never infer it from a voice, name or age guess. Save volunteered facts immediately.

service_unit.description: Caller-supplied unit. An explicit no-unit answer, "just a house" or "single-family home" supports none; do not ask again. Residential alone does not establish the unit. Ask for a missing apartment unit once.

service_zip.description: Five-digit ZIP supplied by caller or returned in the server-prefilled address; do not infer from caller ID.

membership_claim.description: Caller says they have an active maintenance plan (true), explicitly says they do not (false), or is unsure (unknown). This is a claim, not the database membership result. Omit if not discussed.

service_city.description: Caller-supplied city or neighborhood. Filled automatically from a covered NYC ZIP when missing; don't ask for it.

issue_duration.description: Caller-supplied fact; do not invent. Optional notes must not delay urgent handling.

equipment_notes.description: Caller-supplied fact; do not invent. Optional notes must not delay urgent handling.

access_notes.description: Caller-supplied fact; do not invent. Optional notes must not delay urgent handling.

onsite_contact.description: Caller-supplied fact; do not invent. Optional notes must not delay urgent handling.

service_state.description: Two-letter state. Filled automatically (NY) from a covered NYC ZIP; don't ask for it.

callback_number.description: Callback in E.164. Prefer the already saved provider-originating number: ask whether the number they are calling from is best, then confirm the exact saved number. Never guess or update an account phone.

callback_confirmed.description: True only after you read the saved callback back, ended your turn, and the caller said yes in a later turn; never with a changed callback.

preferred_date.description: Requested date in America/New_York; ask to clarify ambiguous dates.

unsafe_to_wait.description: Caller says indoor conditions or a health/safety concern mean they cannot safely wait. A scheduling preference alone is not unsafe. False only for an explicit answer that they can manage; omit if not discussed.

changes.description: Only changed facts. Omit unchanged or undiscussed fields; use unknown for explicitly uncertain risk facts. Do not send nulls.

confirmation_address.description: Required when address_confirmed is true: copy service_address exactly from the latest saved state (or from expected.confirmation_address in an error result).

confirmation_callback.description: Required when callback_confirmed is true: copy callback_number exactly from the latest saved state (or from expected.confirmation_callback in an error result).

bot_say.description: Spoken to the caller while this runs: one brief, natural acknowledgment (2-6 words) that fits this moment, e.g. "Okay, adding that in", "Got it", "Perfect, noting that", "Okay, one second". Vary it from your last one. In the caller's current language. No trailing punctuation.

contents.text: Thanks for bearing with me, I'm still working on it.
Gracias por su paciencia, sigo trabajando en ello.
